A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the iMELD is a promising tool for the prediction of 90-day mortality in liver transplant waiting-list patients.
the MELD score is still the best available tool for the prediction of 90-day mortality in adult liver transplant patients.
the iMELD and the MELD-N score are the most accurate scores for the prediction of 90-day mortality in liver transplant waiting list patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MELD score, as it is currently used, is not an optimal tool to predict the outcome of liver transplantation.
the quality of the development studies of these scores is not sufficient to allow a reliable interpretation and application in clinical practice.
there is no perfect model to assess the risk of death on the liver transplant wait-list, but there are several models that perform well enough to be useful.
